---
title: "On-disk format"
---

## Common metadata fields

Both containers store the same fields, produced by `encode_times`:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `quantization_us` | int | Tick size in microseconds |
| `origin_seconds` | float | First event's absolute time, subtracted before quantization |
| `dtype` | str | Delta array dtype: `uint16`, `uint32`, or `uint64` |
| `n_events` | int | Number of events |
| `max_delta_ticks` | int | Largest single delta, in ticks (omitted for empty trains) |
| `has_labels` | bool | Whether an `event_labels` array is present |

Plus any `extra_meta` passed by the caller (e.g. `pid`, `source`, `recording_id`).

## Blosc directory shard

```text
<path>/
  meta.json                       # metadata + per-array {entry, dtype, shape, nbytes, compressed_nbytes, codec}
  event_times_delta_ticks.blosc   # Blosc(zstd, shuffle)-compressed delta ticks
  event_labels.blosc              # present only if labels were provided
```

Each `.blosc` file is a single opaque Blosc-encoded blob (whole array, no internal
chunking) — decodable only by reading `meta.json` for `dtype`/`shape` first.

## Zarr

```text
<path>.zarr/
  zarr.json                       # group metadata; custom fields (quantization_us, ...) in attributes
  event_times_delta_ticks/
    zarr.json                     # dtype, shape, chunks, codecs=[blosc(zstd, shuffle)]
    c/0                           # chunk data
  event_labels/                   # present only if labels were provided
    zarr.json
    c/0
```

`write_zarr(..., group="rec_a")` nests a train under a named subgroup instead of
the store root, so one store can hold multiple trains as sibling groups.
